proof_summary: For an arbitrary bound, apply the assumed decomposition at \((M+1)!/6\), obtaining \((M+1)!=(6x-1)+(6y+1)\). If the Sophie Germain prime \(6x-1\), or respectively the lower twin prime \(6y-1\), were bounded, then the relevant bounded term (respectively \(6x-1\) or \(6y+1\)) would divide the factorial and hence divide the other prime; primality forces equality or a unit, both incompatible with the positive \(6k\pm1\) forms, so each family contains elements above every bound.
